records.Summary of Oppty: Establishes a $1 fee for registering for the diversity visa lottery.

records.Title: Assuring Responsive and Accountable Federal Executive Management
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule removes the prohibition of a forced distribution of performance rating levels within the Senior Executive Service (SES) and eliminates diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) language within SES performance management regulations.

records.Title: RFI on State Laws Having Significant Adverse Effects on the National Economy or Significant Adverse Effects on Interstate Commerce
records.Summary of Oppty: DOJ is soliciting public comments on State laws significantly and adversely affecting the national economy or interstate commerce along with suggested solutions that could address such effects.

records.Title: Medicare and Medicaid Program Regulations (Accreditation)
records.Summary of Oppty: Among many other provisions, this proposed rule would forbid accrediting institutions from requiring that institutions put in place DEI programs or encourage equity-related programs.

records.Title: Medicare Shared Savings Program Requirements
records.Summary of Oppty: This proposed rule makes scores of changes to Medicare program requirements, including removing health equity benchmarks and adjustments.

records.Title: DOT Strategic Plan
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this RFI, DOT is requesting input on its Strategic Plan for 2026-2030.

records.Title: Reproductive Health Services
records.Summary of Oppty: VA is proposing to reinstate the full exclusion on abortions and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package. The only exclusion to this policy would be “when a physician certifies that the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.”

records.Title: Rescission of Coordinated Enforcement Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is proposing to rescind the regulations that set forth the procedures within the Department for the coordination of enforcement activities by the Wage and Hour Division (WHD), the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and the Employment and Training Administration (ETA) relating to migrant farmworkers. In the Proposed Rule, DOL argues that the regulations should be rescinded because because they limit the Department's discretion, impose unnecessary and duplicative internal procedures, and prevent the Department's agencies from coordinating with regard to migrant farmworkers in more efficient, effective ways.

records.Title: Recission of Final Rule: Improving Protections for Workers in Temporary Agricultural Employment in the United States
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is proposing to rescind provisions of regulations that provide protections for temporary foreign (H-2A visa) agricultural workers. The provisions DOL is proposing to rescind include parts of the regulations addressing worker voice and empowerment, guest access to worker housing, rates of pay and adverse effect wage rates, provision of seatbelts in worker transportation, termination for cause, and document retention and enhanced information collection.

records.Title: Prohibiting Illegal Discrimination in Registered Apprenticeship Programs
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is proposing to rescind a number of non-discrimination provisions in its registered apprenticeship program regulations. Arguing that affirmative action and disparate impact analyses are illegal, DOL proposes to remove provisions related to affirmative action, utilization analysis (on race, sex, ethnicity, and disability), targeted outreach and recruitment, self-identification, apprentice selection, and retaliation.

records.Title: Application of the Fair Labor Standards Act to Domestic Service
records.Summary of Oppty: In 1974, Congress applied FLSA to “domestic service” employees, but exempted employees who provide “companionship services” from the minimum wage and overtime requirements and also exempted live-in domestic service employees from overtime. In 1975, DOL promulgated regulations defining companionship services and permitting third party employers to claim these exemptions. In 2013, DOL revised the regulations to narrow the definition of companionship services and prevent third party employers from claiming either of the exemptions. Because DOL "is concerned that the 2013 regulations might not reflect the best interpretation of the FLSA and might discourage essential companionship services by making these services more expensive, the Department is proposing to return to the 1975 regulations."

records.Title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as Amended
records.Summary of Oppty: VEVRA non-discrimination regulations cross-referenced EO 11246, which prohibited covered contractors from discriminating in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and national origin and required them to take affirmative action. This proposed rule would modify the VEVRA regulations to remove references to EO 11246, effectively leaving veterans status as the only covered basis for a discrimination claim.

records.Title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as Amended
records.Summary of Oppty: Section 503 non-discrimination regulations cross-referenced EO 11246, which prohibited covered contractors from discriminating in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and national origin and required them to take affirmative action. This proposed rule would modify the Section 503 regulations to remove references to EO 11246, effectively limiting the bases for a non-discrimination claim.

records.Title: Rescission of Executive Order 11246 Implementing Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is proposing to rescind the regulations that prohibited covered Federal contractors and subcontractors from discriminating in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and national origin and required them to take affirmative action on those bases. They also prohibited these employers from taking adverse employment actions against applicants or employees because they inquired about, discussed, or disclosed information about their pay or their co-workers' pay, subject to certain limitations.

records.Title: Terminating National Institutes of Health Minority Biomedical Research Support Program and Rescinding the Program's Related Regulation
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this final rule, NIH is terminating the Minority Biomedical Research Support (MBRS) program and repealing related regulations. The MBRS program sought to increase the numbers of ethnic minority faculty, students, and investigators engaged in biomedical research and to broaden the opportunities for participants in biomedical research of ethnic minority faculty, students, and investigator. According to the listing, the "goal of promoting diversity, even if commendable, cannot survive review under equal protection principles."

records.Title: Student Financial Assistance Programs: Negotiated Rulemaking Committee
records.Summary of Oppty: ED is announcing a negotiated rulemaking committee (and seeking nominees to serve on that committee) that will consider student loan limits, simplifying repayment plans, phasing out economic hardship deferments, and other related topics.

records.Title: Buy Now Pay Later Unsecured Debt RFI
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this RFI, HUD seeks public input to better understand the implications of Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) lending on housing affordability and stability. Information gathered in response to this RFI will inform HUD's efforts to ensure that FHA single family mortgage insurance policies effectively address the evolving financial landscape and support the needs of American households.

records.Title: Advancing a Surface Transportation Proposal That Focuses on America's Most Fundamental Infrastructure Needs
records.Summary of Oppty: DOT is requesting feedback on its Surface Transportation Proposal - basically a strategic plan for transportation projects - that focuses on safety, reforming NEPA, increasing technology use, improving economic growth, and strengthening partnerships with states.

records.Title: Anti-Semitism Advisory Committee
records.Summary of Oppty: This committee will provide advice and recommendations to the AG and the DOJ on efforts to combat anti-Semitism across the United States and promote coordinated, timely, and effective responses to anti-Semitism.

records.Title: DOE FOIA “Still Interested” Inquiry
records.Summary of Oppty: Citing proliferation of bot-created FOIA requests, DOE is requiring all FOIA submitters to email the agency to indicate that they're "still interested" in the information they FOIAed.

records.Title: Interpretation of “Federal Public Benefit”
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this notice, HHS redefines "federal public benefit" to restrict access to public benefit programs to individuals with a "qualified" immigration status under PRWORA. Of note, other agencies made the same change but without an opportunity for public comment.

records.Title: RFI on Reducing Regulatory Burdens
records.Summary of Oppty: CPSC provides critical public safety and law enforcement services protecting the public from unreasonable risks of injury or death associated with the use of the thousands of types of consumer products under the agency's jurisdiction. In this RFI, CPSC is seeking input on ways to reduce burdens and costs of its existing rules, regulations, guidance, interpretations, or practices without increasing the risk of death or injury to consumers. According to the listing, "Regulations and other practices that do not reasonably advance safety, but instead promote unscientific ideological agendas, create unnecessary burdens and costs, restrict consumer choice, or reduce competition, entrepreneurship, and innovation—and thereby restrain the American economy—should generally be eliminated or modified."

records.Title: Visa Bond Pilot Program
records.Summary of Oppty: This TFR establishes a temporary visa bond pilot program, which would allow consular officers to offer B-1/B-2 nonimmigrant visas in exchange for a $5, $10, or $15,000 bond if applicants are nationals of countries that the Department has identified: (1) as having high visa overstay rates; (2) where screening and vetting information is deemed deficient; or (3) as offering CBI, if the alien obtained citizenship with no residency requirement.

records.Title: Rescission of the Management and Protection of the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: DOI is proposing to rescind the 2024 regulation restricting oil and gas drilling in the Alaska National Petroleum Reserve area.

records.Title: Statements of General Policy or Interpretation Not Directly Related to Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is removing several provisions from the CFR that it says are "interpretive rules and policy statements regarding the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) which do not carry the force and effect of law." According to the listing, these provisions will be "repurposed as sub-regulatory guidance." Most of the removed provisions address exemptions for various industries from overtime requirements.

records.Title: Rescission of Nondiscrimination and Equal-Opportunity Provisions of the Workforce Investment Act
records.Summary of Oppty: This DFR would rescind DOL's regulations implementing the nondiscrimination and equal-opportunity provisions of WIA. In 2014, Congress passed the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), which repealed WIA and required the Secretary of Labor to transition any authority under WIA to the system created by WIOA. Therefore, the Department is taking this action to remove regulations for a program that is no longer operative. However, it's unclear that WIOA regulations include the same level of detail as this regulation.

records.Title: Rescission of Affirmative Outreach Requirements for Recipients of WIOA Title I Financial Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: This proposed rule would rescind the regulation that requires WIOA recipients to take affirmative outreach efforts to groups based on race, sex, national origin, and other characteristic and provides non-exhaustive examples of actions that may constitute “reasonable efforts.”

records.Title: Imposition and Collection of Civil Penalties for Certain Immigration-Related Violations
records.Summary of Oppty: This IFR would make it easier for DHS to impose civil monetary penalties on undocumented immigrants by (1) removing the "Notice of Intention to Fine" process; (2) shortening the timeline to contest a civil penalty decision; (3) creating a simplified process to contest civil penalties through a written appeal that will be decided by a DHS supervisory immigration officer, rather than the BIA; and (4) allowing DHS to serve civil monetary penalty decisions and orders by ordinary mail.

records.Title: RFI: Federal Agency Collaboration With State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments
records.Summary of Oppty: ACUS is requesting public input on Federal agency approaches and processes for collaborating with State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments when administering Federal programs. Responses to this request may inform an ongoing ACUS project, “Federal Agency Collaboration with State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments” which, if warranted, may recommend best practices for agencies to use.

records.Title: Regulatory Reform
records.Summary of Oppty: DOI seeks comments and information to assist in identifying existing regulations that can be modified or repealed, consistent with applicable law, to ensure that DOI administrative actions do not undermine the national interest and that DOI achieves a meaningful reduction in regulatory burdens while continuing to meet statutory obligations, advance American energy independence, and ensure the responsible stewardship of the Nation's public lands and resources. Note that on 6/24, DOI extended the public comment period for this RFI through 7/21.

records.Title: Suitability and Fitness
records.Summary of Oppty: In this proposed rule, OPM is amending its personnel vetting regulations to increase the speed of adjudications, to clarify that "suitability and fitness" standards apply equally to current employees and applicants, and to more clearly permit adverse actions when a current employee violates suitability and fitness standards. Comment due date extended in this FRN: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-12448

records.Title: Consumer Financial Civil Penalty Fund Rule Amendment
records.Summary of Oppty: CFBP is proposing to amend its 2013 rule that allows Civil Penalty Funds to be used for consumer education and financial literacy programs to the extent victims cannot be located or payments are not practicable. This proposed rule would remove references to allocating funds for consumer education and financial literacy programs.

records.Title: Proposed Sentencing Guideline Priorities for Amendment Cycle
records.Summary of Oppty: In this notice, the US Sentencing Commission is announcing its proposed review priorities for new or revised sentencing guidelines. Proposals are varied and include reviews of certain drug offenses, good behavior adjustments, and sentencing options.

records.Title: Interpretation of “Federal Public Benefit”
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this notice, DOJ redefines "federal public benefit" to restrict access to public benefit programs under PRWORA and describes DOJ's authority to interpret and enforce the law for federal agencies.

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations Related to Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs or Activities (Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Age)
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is proposing to rescind certain regulatory provisions related to nondiscrimination based on age in federally assisted programs or activities. In pertinent part, the rescinded regulation allows for grantees to take "affirmative action to overcome the effects of conditions that resulted in limited participation in the recipient's program or activity on the basis of age."

records.Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Sports Programs Arising Out of Federal Financial Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: Despite receiving significant adverse comments, DOE is not withdrawing its proposed rule, but instead delaying the effective data of the proposed rule.

records.Title: Rescinding New Construction Requirements Related to Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs or Activities
records.Summary of Oppty: Despite receiving significant adverse comments, DOE is not withdrawing its proposed rule, but instead delaying the effective data of the proposed rule.

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations for Loans for Minority Business Enterprises Seeking DOE Contracts and Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: Despite receiving significant adverse comments, DOE is not withdrawing its proposed rule, but instead delaying the effective data of the proposed rule.

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations Related to Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs or Activities (General Provisions)
records.Summary of Oppty: Despite receiving significant adverse comments, DOE is not withdrawing its proposed rule, but instead delaying the effective data of the proposed rule.

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations Related to Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: Despite receiving significant adverse comments, DOE is not withdrawing its proposed rule, but instead delaying the effective data of the proposed rule.

records.Title: RFI: Ensuring Lawful Regulation and Unleashing Innovation To Make American Healthy Again
records.Summary of Oppty: To implement the President's Deregulatory Initiatives and to better promote the health and well-being of the American people HHS is planning the largest deregulatory effort in the history of the Department. To facilitate this effort, HHS seeks input from all interested parties on how to dramatically deregulate across all areas the Department touches. HHS also welcomes other submissions explaining how regulations, guidance, paperwork requirements, and other regulatory obligations can be repealed.

records.Title: Interpretation of “Federal Public Benefit”
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this notice, ED redefines "federal public benefit" to restrict access to public benefit programs, including education loans like Perkins loans to individuals with a "qualified" immigration status under PRWORA.

records.Title: Interpretation of “Federal Public Benefit”
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this notice, USDA redefines "federal public benefit" to restrict access to public benefit programs, including SNAP, WIC, and school lunches to individuals with a "qualified" immigration status under PRWORA.

records.Title: Removal of Unconstitutional Preferences Based on Race and Sex in Response to Court Ruling
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this final rule, USDA announces that it will no longer employ the race- and sex-based “socially disadvantaged” designation to provide increased benefits based on race and sex to the programs noted in the final rule, which include a number of its loan and grant programs.

records.Title: Employment of Workers With Disabilities Under Section 14(c) of the Fair Labor Standards Act; Withdrawal
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is withdrawing a 2024 proposed rule that would have phased out the issuance of subminimum wage certificates, which allow companies to pay a wage rate below the minimum wage to certain employees with disabilities.

records.Title: Pipeline Safety: Amendments to Liquefied Natural Gas Facilities
records.Summary of Oppty: This ANPRM solicits stakeholder feedback on potential opportunities for amendment of its regulations governing the siting, design, installation, construction, inspection, testing, operation, and maintenance of LNG facilities.

records.Title: Rescission of Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: This proposed rule would rescind the HUD's Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing regulations, which require a participant in an FHA insurance or Multifamily Housing rental assistance program to complete and submit a form supplied by HUD that describes its affirmative fair housing marketing plan.

records.Title: Recission of Voter Registration Notice
records.Summary of Oppty: Rescinds a 1996 notice that provided guidance on efforts by Public Housing Agencies to promote voter registration in Public and Indian Housing.

records.Title: RFI on Prescription Drug Machine-Readable File Requirement in the Transparency in Coverage Final Rule
records.Summary of Oppty: This RFI is intended to gather input regarding implementation of the prescription drug machine-readable file disclosure requirements under the Transparency in Coverage final rules, including what modifications to the disclosure requirements or additional technical implementation guidance might be necessary to better ensure the accurate and timely completion of the prescription drug file.

records.Title: Rescinding Unnecessary Notice and Comment Procedures
records.Summary of Oppty: DOL is rescinding a 1971 regulation that waived APA notice and comment rulemaking exceptions for DOL regulations related to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts. DOL will now take advantage of the APA exemption, following the notice and comment process for only a subset of its regulations.

records.Title: Construction Standards-Advisory Committee on Construction Safety and Health
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule revokes an earlier regulation that required the Assistant Secretary for Occupational Safety and Health, who heads OSHA, to consult with the Advisory Committee on Construction Safety and Health (ACCSH) in the formulation of rules to promulgate, modify, or revoke standards applicable to construction work and the general OSHA regulations governing ACCSH. The FR argues that the consultation requirement is more burdensome than mandated by statute and that compliance with these regulations would needlessly delay the Secretary of Labor's regulatory agenda.

records.Title: RFI Related to the Executive Order, “Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account”
records.Summary of Oppty: Treasury is seeking input on implementation of the EO which, among other items, directs the Treasury to cease issuing paper checks and transition to the use of electronic payments for all Federal disbursements where feasible. Treasury seeks input especially on efforts to advance a public awareness campaign that will help consumers, including unbanked and underbanked populations, transition to digital payments as contemplated by the E.O.

records.Title: Updates to the Medicare Quality Reporting Program for Federal Fiscal Year 2026
records.Summary of Oppty: This proposed rule would change and update policies and payment rates used under the Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) Prospective Payment System (PPS) for FY 2026. Among many other changes, this rule proposes updates to the Skilled Nursing Facility Value-Based Purchasing (SNF VBP) Program, including removing the Health Equity Adjustment, estimating performance standards, applying the Program's scoring methodology to the Skilled Nursing Facility Within-Stay Potentially Preventable Readmission (SNF WS PPR) measure, adopting a new reconsideration process that will allow SNFs to appeal CMS's decisions on review and correction requests, and technical updates to the SNF VBP Program's regulation text.

records.Title: RFI Regarding Foreign Nations Freeloading on American-Financed Innovation
records.Summary of Oppty: USTR invites comments from interested parties regarding any act, policy, or practice that may be unreasonable or discriminatory and that has the effect of forcing American patients to pay for a disproportionate amount of global pharmaceutical research and development, including by suppressing the price of pharmaceutical products below fair market value in foreign countries.

records.Title: ACA Marketplace Integrity and Affordability
records.Summary of Oppty: Among many other provisions, this final rule revises standards relating to denial of coverage for failure to pay past-due premium; excludes Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients from the definition of “lawfully present;” revises standards related to the annual open enrollment period and special enrollment periods; revises standards relating to income eligibility verifications for premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions, annual eligibility redeterminations, de minimis thresholds for the actuarial value for plans subject to essential health benefits (EHB) requirements, and income-based cost-sharing reduction plan variations. This final rule also revises the premium adjustment percentage methodology and prohibits issuers of coverage subject to EHB requirements from providing coverage for specified gender affirming care procedures as an EHB.

records.Title: Guidance on Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
records.Summary of Oppty: Generally sets policy on regulatory enforcement aligned with EO on Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations and announces it will report to OMB by May 9, 2026 on "(1) a list of all criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by the Department; and (2) for each such criminal regulatory offense, the range of potential criminal penalties for a violation and the applicable mens rea standard for the criminal regulatory offense."

records.Title: Guidance on Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
records.Summary of Oppty: Generally sets policy on regulatory enforcement aligned with EO on Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations and announces it will report to OMB by May 9, 2026 on "(1) a list of all criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by the Department; and (2) for each such criminal regulatory offense, the range of potential criminal penalties for a violation and the applicable mens rea standard for the criminal regulatory offense."

records.Title: Strengthening Probationary Periods in the Federal Service
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule resciends OPM regulations on probationary periods in the competitive service and creates new standards for certifying the value of a probationary employee at the end of their probation period. This rule did not follow a standard APA process - there was no proposed rule or opportunity for public comment. The rule indicates that because the Probationary Employees EO directed the recission of the prior regulations, no public comment process was necessary.

records.Title: Exploration of "Health Level Seven Fast" Healthcare Interoperability Resources for Use in Study Data Created From Real-World Data Sources for Submission to the FDA
records.Summary of Oppty: The FDA is establishing a docket for public comments exploring the Health Level Seven (HL7) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) for submission of data collected from real-world data sources. In alignment with the new HHS health IT policy. FDA is exploring approaches to optimize the submission of structured and standardized clinical study data collected from RWD sources. FDA is seeking public comment from interested parties on several specific questions.

records.Title: Proposed Priorities and Definitions-Secretary's Supplemental Priorities and Definitions on Evidence-Based Literacy, Education Choice, and Returning Education to the States
records.Summary of Oppty: This listing proposes three initial and urgent priorities and related definitions for use in currently authorized discretionary grant programs or programs that may be authorized in the future. ED proposes prioritizing Promoting Evidence-Based Literacy (new definitions of evidence-based and related terms included in the listing), Expanding Education Choice (focusing on charter schools and apprenticeships), and Returning Education to the States.

records.Title: Guidance on Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
records.Summary of Oppty: Generally sets policy on regulatory enforcement aligned with EO on Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations and announces it will report to OMB by May 9, 2026 on "(1) a list of all criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by the Department; and (2) for each such criminal regulatory offense, the range of potential criminal penalties for a violation and the applicable mens rea standard for the criminal regulatory offense."

records.Title: Protocol for the Pathways to Work Evidence Clearinghouse: Methods and Standards, Version 2.0
records.Summary of Oppty: Pathways to Work seeks to be a comprehensive resource that a range of audiences, including State and local Temporary Assistance for Needy Families administrators, can use to identify the services that will best help people with low incomes succeed in the labor market. Pathways to Work carries out a systematic process to identify, review, and rate the quality of eligible studies of programs and policies that have the primary aim of improving the employment and earnings of people with low incomes. The process is implemented by trained reviewers using consistent and transparent standards and procedures. The draft Protocol Version 2.0 aims to revise existing standards and to add new standards for including and rating the quality of program cost studies.

records.Title: Federal Restoration of Gun Rights: Withdrawing the Attorney General's Delegation of Authority
records.Summary of Oppty: Under a 1968 law, a "person who is prohibited from possessing, shipping, transporting, or receiving firearms or ammunition may make application to the Attorney General for relief from th[at] disabilit[y]." The AG delegated that authority to ATF, which has been prohibited from exercising that power through a Congressional appropriations rider for about 30 years. This notice withdraws the delegation to ATF so that the authority to adjudicate applications for relief from gun possession prohibitions once again lies with the AG. The IFR suggests that regulations for creating an application for relief are forthcoming from DOJ.

records.Title: Guidance on Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
records.Summary of Oppty: Generally sets policy on regulatory enforcement aligned with EO on Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations and announces it will report to OMB by May 9, 2026 on "(1) a list of all criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by the Department; and (2) for each such criminal regulatory offense, the range of potential criminal penalties for a violation and the applicable mens rea standard for the criminal regulatory offense."

records.Title: RFI: Health Technology Ecosystem
records.Summary of Oppty: This RFI seeks input from the public regarding the market of digital health products for Medicare beneficiaries as well as the state of data interoperability and broader health technology infrastructure. Responses to this RFI may be used to inform CMS and ASTP/ONC efforts to lead infrastructure progress to cultivate this market, increasing beneficiary access to effective digital capabilities needed to make informed health decisions, and increasing data availability for all stakeholders contributing to health outcomes.

records.Title: Rescinding Reporting Requirements, Certification, Independent Verification, and DOE Review for Voluntary Greenhouse Gas Reporting
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is proposing to rescind reporting requirements, certification, independent verification, and DOE review for the Voluntary Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program. DOE seeks all comments on any aspects of this proposal.

records.Title: Renewable Energy Production Incentives
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is proposing to rescind the Renewable Energy Production Incentives program regulations at the end of fiscal year 2026. DOE's proposal is intended to parallel the program's statutory sunset date. The Department seeks comments on any reason to rescind or not rescind these regulations.

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations Related to Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule rescinds certain unnecessary regulatory provisions related to nondiscrimination on the basis of sex in education programs or activities receiving federal financial assistance. Note that because this is a direct final rule, the agency is required to withdraw it if it receives adverse comment (though the DFR defines "significant adverse comment," that is not the appropriate legal standard).

records.Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Sports Programs Arising Out of Federal Financial Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: This DFR amends existing regulations requiring certain funding recipients that sponsor sports teams for members of one sex to allow members of the opposite sex to try out for the team. Accordingly, these requirements will no longer be a factor when recipients operate sports teams. Note that because this is a direct final rule, the agency is required to withdraw it if it receives adverse comment (though the DFR defines "significant adverse comment," that is not the appropriate legal standard).

records.Title: Rescinding New Construction Requirements Related to Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs or Activities
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE issued a regulation requiring new construction to comply with accessibility standards. This DFR rescinds certain new construction requirements related to disability nondiscrimination in federally assisted programs or activities. Note that because this is a direct final rule, the agency is required to withdraw it if it receives adverse comment (though the DFR defines "significant adverse comment," that is not the appropriate legal standard).

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations for Loans for Minority Business Enterprises Seeking DOE Contracts and Assistance
records.Summary of Oppty: This DFR rescinds a regulation which sets forth policies and procedures for the award and administration of loans to minority business enterprises. According to the listing, DOE believes this regulation "violates the Secretary's policy to treat people without regard to the color of their skin. Contrary to this policy, the regulations identify groups based on their race, sort them, and intentionally deliver preferences based on the resulting groups. Even if such regulations were constitutional, DOE would rescind them."

records.Title: Rescinding Regulations Related to Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs or Activities (General Provisions)
records.Summary of Oppty: This direct final rule rescinds certain unnecessary regulatory provisions related to nondiscrimination in federally assisted programs or activities. Note that because this is a direct final rule, the agency is required to withdraw it if it receives adverse comment (though the DFR defines "significant adverse comment," that is not the appropriate legal standard).

records.Title: Administrative Rulemaking, Guidance, and Enforcement Procedures
records.Summary of Oppty: The reforms proposed in this NPRM set forth (1) updated policies and procedures governing the development and issuance of regulations by the Department's operating administrations and components of the Office of the Secretary; (2) enhanced procedures for the review and clearance of guidance documents; and (3) improved procedural requirements governing the Department's administrative enforcement actions and judicial enforcement actions brought in Federal court, including express rights of regulated parties to enforce the protections proposed in this NPRM through administrative proceedings.

records.Title: Request for Information and Comments on the Preparation of the 11th National Outer Continental Shelf Oil and Gas Leasing Program
records.Summary of Oppty: The OCS Lands Act declares that it is the policy of the United States that the OCS “is a vital national resource reserve held by the Federal Government for the public, which should be made available for expeditious and orderly development, subject to environmental safeguards, in a manner which is consistent with the maintenance of competition and other national needs.” BOEM requests information and comments from Tribal, state, and local governments, Native American and Native Alaskan organizations, Federal agencies, environmental and other public interest organizations, the oil and gas industry, non-energy industries, other interested organizations and entities, and the public, for use in the preparation of the 11th National OCS Program.

records.Title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Rescission of Changes to Civil Rights Data Collection Methods
records.Summary of Oppty: In December 2023, SNAP issued a rule that prohibited using visual observation as a data collection method for race and ethnicity. It also removed regulatory language that provides an example that State agencies might collect race and ethnicity data by observation (also referred to as “visual observation”) when participants do not voluntarily provide the information on the application form. FNS is proposing to rescind the rule and seek comment on that proposal.

records.Title: Notice of Enforcement Discretion: Ensuring Safe Accommodations for Air Travelers With Disabilities Using Wheelchairs
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces that DOT will not take enforcement action against entities for failing to comply with the requirements contained in the Ensuring Safe Accommodations for Air Travelers With Disabilities Using Wheelchairs regulation (Wheelchair Rule) through Aug. 1, 2025.

records.Title: Medicare Program; FY 2026 Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Prospective Payment System-Rate Update
records.Summary of Oppty: This rulemaking proposes to update the prospective payment rates, the outlier threshold, and the wage index for Medicare inpatient hospital services provided by Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities (IPFs), which include psychiatric hospitals and excluded psychiatric units of an acute care hospital or critical access hospital. Changes include removing COVID, equity, and gender from all related documents.

records.Title: Medicare Program; Hospital Inpatient Prospective Payment Systems for Acute Care Hospitals and the Long-Term Care Hospital Prospective Payment System and Policy Changes and Fiscal Year 2026 Rates; Requirements for Quality Programs; and Other Policy Changes
records.Summary of Oppty: This would revise the Medicare hospital inpatient prospective payment systems (IPPS) for operating and capital-related costs of acute care hospitals; make changes relating to Medicare graduate medical education (GME) for teaching hospitals; update the payment policies and the annual payment rates for the Medicare prospective payment system (PPS) for inpatient hospital services provided by long-term care hospitals (LTCHs); update and make changes to requirements for certain quality programs; and make other policy-related changes. Many of the proposed changes include removing references to race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, and gender identity wherever they appear, including in assessments, data collection, and planning documents.

records.Title: Medicare Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System for Federal Fiscal Year 2026 and Updates to the IRF Quality Reporting Program
records.Summary of Oppty: Among other changes, this rule proposes to remove two quality measures on COVID coverage and to remove four Standardized Patient Assessment Data Elements under the Social Determinant of Health (SDOH) category

records.Title: Guidance on Referrals for Potential Criminal Enforcement
records.Summary of Oppty: Per the EO on Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, USDA is announcing a general policy that it will consider factors like knowledge of the law and risk of harm when deciding whether to refer violations of regulations to DOJ for criminal prosecution. The notice also provides a timeline for when it will provide a list of all criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by the agency or the DOJ and describe the applicable statutory authorities, the range of potential criminal penalties for a violation, and the applicable mens rea standard for the criminal regulatory offense.

records.Title: Protection of Federal Property
records.Summary of Oppty: This regulation transfers authority to protect federal property from GSA to DHS. In addition, it provides charging options for violations occurring on and adjacent to Federal property, update prohibited conduct to incorporate advancing technology, provide clearer public notice, and apply the regulations more uniformly to property owned, operated or secured by the Federal Government. Notably, this rule was proposed during the Biden Administration.

records.Title: Rescissions Proposals Pursuant to the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice formally announces rescission proposals for $9.4 billion of programs of the Department of State, as well as the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), the U.S. Institute of Peace, and other International Assistance Programs. According to the listing, "rescissions would eliminate programs that are antithetical to American interests, such as funding the World Health Organization, “family planning” and “reproductive health,” LGBTQI+ activities, “equity” programs, radical Green New Deal-type policies, and color revolutions in hostile places around the world. In addition, Federal spending on CPB subsidizes a public media system that is politically biased and is an unnecessary expense to the taxpayer."

records.Title: Improving Performance, Accountability and Responsiveness in the Civil Service
records.Summary of Oppty: OPM is is proposing a rule to formally adopt "Schedule Poilcy/Career" employment category, which lets policy-influencing positions be moved into Schedule Policy/Career. According to the rule, "These positions will remain career jobs filled on a nonpartisan basis." However, the rule turns these career civil service positions into at-will positions excepted from adverse action procedures or appeals. This will allow agencies to quickly remove employees from critical positions who engage in misconduct, perform poorly, or undermine the democratic process by intentionally subverting Presidential directives. Deadline for comments extended to June 7 through this notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-09356

records.Title: Assuring Responsive and Accountable Federal Executive Management
records.Summary of Oppty: OPM is proposing to remove the prohibition of a forced distribution of performance rating levels within the Senior Executive Service (SES) as well as eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) language within SES performance management regulations. According to the listing, "Removing the prohibition on forced distribution would allow agencies to establish and enforce limits on the highest SES rating levels, thereby increasing rigor in the SES appraisal process and leading to a more normalized distribution of SES ratings across the Federal Government."

records.Title: Negotiated Rulemaking on Student Loan Repayment Programs
records.Summary of Oppty: Among other technical questions, the Student Loans and Affordability Committee will address Refining definitions of a qualifying employer for the purposes of determining eligibility for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program and revisiting family size, restructuring repayment plan provisions, including the alternative repayment plan, and certain other provisions of the July 10, 2023 rule. Nominees for negotiators should be from civil rights orgs, states, military, higher ed (incl HBCUs), financial aid admins, taxpayer orgs, or FFEL lenders.

records.Title: Sentencing Guidelines for US Courts
records.Summary of Oppty: Notice and request for comment on amendments to the Sentencing Guidelines, which include more clearly defining what constitutes "other uses" of a firearm and what constitutes "physical restraint;" as well as changes to how mitigation is calculated in drug trafficking cases. The amendments also allow for greater discretion in the use of supervised release.

records.Title: Request for Information on the Development of a 2025 National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Research and Development (R&D) Strategic Plan
records.Summary of Oppty: NSF welcomes input from all interested parties on how the previous administration's National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan can be rewritten so that the United States can secure its position as the unrivaled world leader in artificial intelligence by performing R&D to accelerate AI-driven innovation, enhance U.S. economic and national security, promote human flourishing, and maintain the United States' dominance in AI while focusing on the Federal government's unique role in AI R&D over the next 3 to 5 years.

records.Title: Energy Conservation Standards for Manufactured Housing
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is proposing to amend the compliance date for its manufactured housing energy conservation standards. Currently, manufacturers must comply with these standards on and after July 1, 2025, for Tier 2 homes and 60 days after the issuance of enforcement procedures for Tier 1 homes. DOE is proposing to delay the Tier 2 compliance date to allow DOE more time to consider the proposed enforcement procedures and comments submitted, and to evaluate appropriate next steps that provide clarity for manufacturers and other stakeholders.

records.Title: Unaccompanied Children Program Foundational Rule; Update To Accord With Statutory Requirements
records.Summary of Oppty: This IFR removes a provision from the UAC Foundational Rule that precludes ORR from "shar[ing] any immigration status information relating to potential sponsors with any law enforcement or immigration enforcement related entity at any time.” According to the IRR, this provision conflicts with the underlying federal statute and should therefore be rescinded.

records.Title: Draft Aquaculture Opportunity Area Options-Alaska State Waters
records.Summary of Oppty: NOAA is proposing Aquaculture Opportunity Area (AOA) Options within State waters of southeast, southcentral, and southwest Alaska as part of the AOA identification process. An AOA is a defined geographic area that has been evaluated to determine its potential suitability for commercial aquaculture per the Seafood Competitiveness EO. This notice invites public comment on the preliminary results of the marine spatial planning study including the identification of draft AOA Options in Alaska State waters. NMFS will consider information received in response to this notice when finalizing the results of the marine spatial planning study, and may or may not identify AOAs after further public participation and review under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).

records.Title: Terminology Relating to Sex; Technical Amendments
records.Summary of Oppty: This technical amendment replaces the term “gender” with “sex” wherever it appears in TSA's regulations.

records.Title: Rescinding the Definition of “Harm” Under the Endangered Species Act
records.Summary of Oppty: FWS is proposing to rescind the regulatory definition of “harm” in our Endangered Species Act regulations. According to the listing, the existing regulatory definition of “harm,” which includes habitat modification, runs contrary to the best meaning of the statutory term “take.” ESA asserts it is "undertaking this change to adhere to the single, best meaning of the ESA."

records.Title: Rescinded Guidance Materials
records.Summary of Oppty: Per the deregulation EO, DOE is rescinding a number of guidance documents, primarily focused on climate resilience and clean energy.

records.Title: Eliminating Unnecessary Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: Pursuant to an Executive order, Treasury is conducting a review of existing regulations, with the goal of reducing regulatory burden by revoking or revising existing regulations that meet the criteria set forth in the Executive order. In support of that objective, this direct final rule streamlines titles 12 and 31 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) by removing regulations that are no longer necessary or no longer have any current or future applicability. These include regulations related to Federal Financing Banks, TARP regulations, and a civil penalty regulation.

records.Title: Experiences With FEMA Disaster Responses
records.Summary of Oppty: The FEMA Review Council seeks comments from the public and other interested stakeholders to gain an understanding of their experience with FEMA during disasters. The questions the FEMARC would especially like information about are generally about FEMA response time and efficiency, difficulties in applying for benefits, whether state/local/private groups provided more timely assistance than FEMA, and any recommendations commenters have for the Council.

records.Title: Notification of HHS Documents Identified for Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: HHS is rescinding four informal guidance documents on COVID, opioids, and LGBTQ protections.

records.Title: Reducing the Size of the Board of Immigration Appeals
records.Summary of Oppty: This IFR would reduce the number of members of the Board of Immigration Appeals from 28 to 15. Historically, people have argued that a larger number of board members will result in a faster disposition of the BIA's large backlog; this notice suggests that a smaller Board will increase cohesiveness in decisionmaking.

records.Title: Privacy Act of 1974; Exempting a System of Records From Certain Requirements
records.Summary of Oppty: Treasury is exempting the IRS Insider Risk Management SOR from certain provisions of the Privacy Act. Basically, many provisions of that law allow people to know when their record is shared with another agency, allow amendment or appeal of their records, allow them to know if they're in a record, etc. This rule provides exemptions to all those provisions on the grounds that knowing they're in the record could impede an investigation against a person.

records.Title: Removal of Obsolete Crop Assistance Program Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: Pursuant to UDA's regulatory review, FSA is updating our regulations to remove the FSA Crop Assistance Program (CAP), which is obsolete. The changes in this rule will have no impacts on past or present FSA customers.

records.Title: Child and Adult Care Food Program: Rescission of Obsolete Data Collection Requirements
records.Summary of Oppty: This rule rescinds an obsolete data collection requirement in regulations regarding the Child and Adult Care Food Program pursuant to USDA's regulatory review. On its face, this seems to be a truly unnecessary regulation.

records.Title: Withdrawal: Interpretive Rules, Policy Statements, and Advisory Opinions
records.Summary of Oppty: CFPB is withdrawing dozens of policy statements, interpretive rules, and advisory opinions pursuant to the deregulation and guidance Executive Orders. This includes regulatory documents on many consumer protection issues, as well as documents prohibiting discrimination on the basis of SOGI, TILA and debt collection regulations, whistleblower protections, PSLF and Section 8 rules, and more.

records.Title: RFI: Deregulation
records.Summary of Oppty: Through this RFI, OMB is soliciting ideas for deregulation from across the country. Commenters should identify rules to be rescinded and provide detailed reasons for their rescission. OMB invites comments about any and all regulations currently in effect.

records.Title: Withdrawal of Notices Inviting Application and Cancellation of the Competitions for the Fulbright-Hays Group Projects Abroad (GPA) Program, Doctoral Dissertation Research Abroad (DDRA) Program, and Faculty Research Abroad (FRA) Fellowship Program
records.Summary of Oppty: ED is withdrawing the notice inviting applications for FY 2025 for the Fulbright-Hays Group Projects Abroad Program, Doctoral Dissertation Research Abroad Program, and the Faculty Research Abroad Fellowship Program. According to the listing, The Department is cancelling the competitions as part of a comprehensive review of recently published FY 2025 NIAs. This reevaluation seeks to ensure that all priorities and requirements for the Department's FY 2025 competitions align with the objectives established by the Trump Administration, foster consistency across all grant programs, and enhance the economic effectiveness of federal education funding.

records.Title: Recission: Federal Management Regulation; Nondiscrimination Clarification in the Federal Workplace
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA's 2016 bulletin concludes that sex discrimination under relevant Federal laws also included discrimination based on gender identity and gender status. GSA is rescinding the bulletin pursuant to the Transgender EO. This is especially relevant because it arguably precludes access to bathrooms including gender inclusive bathrooms in all federal buildings.

records.Title: Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Revisions
records.Summary of Oppty: In this IFR, HUD is removing the requirements for PHAs to conduct an Analysis of Impediments to fair housing (AI) or any other form of assessment tool - including the requirement to assess any group's disproportionate need for housing supports. Instead, PHAs will simply need to submit a certification that they intend to take some sort of action to further fair housing. This also applies to AFFH requirements in related programs, such as HOPWA, ESG, etc. Note that submission date was extended to 5/9 in this notice: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-07961

records.Title: Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure on DOE Lands
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE seeks to enable the construction of AI infrastructure at select DOE sites to begin by the end of 2025, with a target of commencing operation by the end of 2027. This RFI seeks to assess industry interest in developing, operating, and maintaining AI infrastructure on select DOE owned or managed lands, along with information on potential development approaches, technology solutions, operational models, and economic considerations associated with establishing AI infrastructure on DOE sites. In addition, this RFI seeks input from grid operators that serve DOE sites on opportunities and challenges associated with existing energy infrastructure and potential co-location of data centers with new energy generation.

records.Title: Withdrawal of Notice Inviting Applications (NIA) and Cancellation of the Competition for the Native American Career and Technical Education Program (NACTEP)
records.Summary of Oppty: ED is withdrawing this NIA as part of a comprehensive review of recently published FY 2025 NIAs. This reevaluation seeks to ensure that all priorities and requirements for the Department's FY 2025 competitions align with the objectives established by the Trump Administration while fostering consistency across all grant programs.

records.Title: Withdrawal of Notice Inviting Applications (NIA) and Cancellation of the Competition for the Native Hawaiian Career and Technical Education Program (NHCTEP)
records.Summary of Oppty: ED is withdrawing this NIA as part of a comprehensive review of recently published FY 2025 NIAs. This reevaluation seeks to ensure that all priorities and requirements for the Department's FY 2025 competitions align with the objectives established by the Trump Administration while fostering consistency across all grant programs.

records.Title: Withdrawal: Energy Conservation Program Determination of Miscellaneous Gas Products as a Covered Consumer Product
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is withdrawing its prior determination that miscellaneous gas products (“MGPs”), which include decorative hearths and outdoor heaters, qualify as covered products under Part A of Title III of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, as amended (“EPCA”).

records.Title: Stay: Clean Energy for New Federal Buildings and Major Renovations of Federal Buildings
records.Summary of Oppty: In May 2024, DOE issued regulations that require certain new Federal buildings and Federal buildings undergoing major renovations to be designed to reduce their fossil fuel-generated energy consumption and provides a process for Federal agencies to petition for a downward adjustment from these requirements if applicable. DOE is currently reviewing the recent implementation guidance and the template for petitions for downward adjustments to ensure that they are consistent with the policies of the current Administration. Accordingly, DOE stays the compliance date of the recent final rule.

records.Title: Negotiated Rulemaking on Student Loan Repayment Programs
records.Summary of Oppty: ED intends to conduct public hearings and establish one or more negotiated rulemaking committees to prepare proposed regulations on various programs authorized under title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended (HEA) (title IV, HEA programs). The Department invites public feedback, especially addressing topics which may include Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), Pay As You Earn (PAYE), Income-Contingent Repayment (ICR), or other topics that would streamline current federal student financial assistance programs.

records.Title: Ensuring Lawful Regulation; Reducing Regulation and Controlling Regulatory Costs
records.Summary of Oppty: Pursuant to the "deregulation EO," DOT seeks comments and information to assist DOT in identifying existing regulations, guidance, paperwork requirements, and other regulatory obligations that can be modified or repealed, consistent with law, to ensure that DOT administrative actions do not undermine the national interest and that DOT achieves meaningful burden reduction while continuing to meet statutory obligations and ensure the safety of the U.S. transportation system. The RFI includes a number of specific questions related to its programs and policies.

records.Title: Policy Regarding Obtaining Information From, or Records of, Members of the News Media; and Regarding Questioning, Arresting, or Charging Members of the News Media
records.Summary of Oppty: Rescinds Biden-era policy on the use of law enforcement tools (e.g., subpeonas, court orders) to obtain information from the media and on prosecuting media for noncompliance with subpeonas.

records.Title: Sentencing Guidelines for US Courts
records.Summary of Oppty: USSC is considering several sentencing guideline enhancements that would increase penalties for offenses involving fentanyl and other synthetic opiods.

records.Title: Withdrawal: Policy Statement on the Treatment of Environmental Justice Matters in NRC Regulatory and Licensing Actions; Environmental Justice Strategy
records.Summary of Oppty: To comply with the environmental justice/DEI EO, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is withdrawing its Policy Statement on the Treatment of Environmental Justice Matters in NRC Regulatory and Licensing Actions (Environmental Justice Policy Statement) and its Environmental Justice Strategy.

records.Title: Granting of Relief; Federal Firearms Privileges
records.Summary of Oppty: Restores gun rights to 10 people, including Mel Gibson and an NFL star. Critics have suggested these restorations are unethical.

records.Title: Withrawal: Proposed Salmonella Framework for Raw Poultry Products
records.Summary of Oppty: Withdraws proposed rule on salmonella that requirde that all poultry slaughter establishments develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to prevent contamination. Due to feedback from producers, USDA is withdrawing the rule to allow the Agency to further assess its approach for addressing Salmonella illnesses associated with poultry products.

records.Title: Presidential Memorandum; Preventing Illegal Aliens From Obtaining Social Security Act Benefits
records.Summary of Oppty: Apparently a republication of the PM issued 4/15. Likely to meet a legal publication requirement.

records.Title: Notice of Designation of Policy-Making Positions; Later Withdrawn
records.Summary of Oppty: The Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board has determined that the Deputy General Counsel position is of a policy-determining and policy-advocating character and is not normally subject to change as a result of a Presidential transition. Accordingly, this position is designated as a Schedule Policy/Career position. Withdrawl notice subsequently issued: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-07532

records.Title: Waters of the United States
records.Summary of Oppty: EPA seeks input on the Waters of the US regulation, which defines which waterways are subject to federal control and regulation. This rule has been revised a number of times; the last broad revision was the subject of a SCOTUS ruling in 2023; this RFI asks for input on how to interpret some of the language in the SCOTUS ruling, including the phrases "relatively permanent" and "continuous surface connection." The RFI also indicates that EPA will hold six listening sessions on this topic throughout April and May.

records.Title: Withdrawal of Direct Final Rule: Name Change From Office of Child Support Enforcement to Office of Child Support Services
records.Summary of Oppty: ACF issued a direct final rule changing the name of the Office of Child Support enforcement. On February 27, 2025, ACF re-opened the comment period and delayed the effective date until April 28, 2025. The comment period closed March 31, 2025. ACF is withdrawing the direct final rule because the Agency received significant adverse comment.

records.Title: Notice of Rescission of Report on Lawful Uses of Race or Sex in Federal Contracting Programs
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces that the prior guidance in Notice of Report on Lawful Uses of Race or Sex in Federal Contracting Programs, published in the Federal Register on January 31, 2022, is "no longer considered an accurate reflection of the current laws, executive orders, and federal court jurisprudence concerning the constitutionality of using race or sex in federal government programs and should not be cited in the defense of them."

records.Title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule
records.Summary of Oppty: This document Federal Trade Commission amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule. The amendments to the Rule include one new definition and modifications to several others, as well as updates to key provisions to respond to changes in technology and online practices. The amendments are intended to strengthen protection of personal information collected from children, and, where appropriate, to clarify and streamline the Rule since it was last amended in January 2013.

records.Title: Assessing Performance of the National Highway System, Greenhouse Gas Emissions Measure
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule repeals a requirement that State departments of transportation and metropolitan planning organizations establish declining carbon dioxide (CO2) targets for the greenhouse gas measure and report on progress toward the achievement of the target.

records.Title: Termination of the Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program
records.Summary of Oppty: Formally terminates the Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program, which was paused on January 28, 2025.

records.Title: Implementation of the National Suicide Hotline Act of 2018
records.Summary of Oppty: FCC seeks input on proposed strategies for georouting text messages sent to 988 so that local crisis centers will be able to respond. Prior public comment periods resulted in several proposed strategies for enabling georouting while protecting the privacy of 988 users; this public comment period seeks additional input on those proposed strategies.

records.Title: Delay of Effective Date for 2 Final Regulations
records.Summary of Oppty: Delays the effective date of two rules on water quality and sewage sludge.

records.Title: HOME Investment Partnerships Program: Program Updates and Streamlining-Delay of Effective Date, Withdrawal, and Correction
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice further delays the effective date of some provisions of the HOME rule, which was issued in January 2025. Other provisions are completely withdrawn (without notice and comment) and others are allowed to become effective.

records.Title: Order Suspending the Application of Section 1-402 or 1-404 of Executive Order 12171
records.Summary of Oppty: Exempts several VA unions from the Executive Order on collective bargaining agreements.

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Art in Architecture; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA plans to issue a final rule rescinding the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2021-02, “Art in Architecture,” published on February 2, 2022. GSA will amend the FMR to update certain provisions of the Art in Architecture program to remove diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) language, preferential treatments, and DEI data collections.

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Designation of Authority and Sustainable Siting; Planned Revision
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA plans to issue a final rule revising the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2023-102-1, “Designation of Authority and Sustainable Siting” published on April 22, 2024. GSA will amend the Federal Management Regulation Location of Space to remove sustainability and diversity, equity, and inclusion language.

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Federal Advisory Committee Management; Planned Revision
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA plans to issue a final rule revising the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2022-01, “Federal Advisory Committee Management,” published on April 18, 2024. GSA will amend the FMR to apply these revisions to the Federal Advisory Committee Management regulation in order to align the regulation with current Administration priorities, improve Federal advisory committee management policies and processes, remove unnecessary language and information, and reduce (or eliminate where possible) unnecessary administrative burdens on executive branch agencies and departments.

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Soliciting Union Memberships Among Contractors in GSA-Controlled Buildings; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA plans to issue a final rule rescinding the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2022-02, “Soliciting Union Memberships Among Contractors in GSA-Controlled Buildings,” published on September 2, 2022. This upcoming rule will clarify that activities related to worker organizing and collective bargaining among contractors' employees working in Federal Government facilities are covered or restricted by the general prohibition on soliciting, posting, and distributing materials in or on Federal property under the jurisdiction, custody, or control of GSA (GSA-controlled property).

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Updating Transportation Management, With Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: GSA plans to issue a final rule rescinding Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2024-03, “Federal Management Regulation; Updating Transportation Management, With Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language,” published on November 26, 2024. GSA will amend the FMR to ensure compliance with the current Administration's priorities, to remove unnecessary language, and to revert language back to sex-specific pronouns.

records.Title: Federal Management Regulation; Updating the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) With Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: Announces that GSA will be issuing a final rule partly rescinding the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) Case 2024-01, “Updating the Federal Management Regulation (FMR) with Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language,” published on August 22, 2024. GSA will amend FMR parts 102-5 and 102-33 through 102-42 to replace non-gendered pronouns with gendered pronouns and to remove diversity, equity, and inclusion language inserted by the previous administration.

records.Title: Federal Travel Regulation; Alternative Fuel Vehicle Usage During Relocations; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces that GSA plans to issue a final rule rescinding Federal Travel Regulation (FTR) Case 2022-03, “Alternative Fuel Vehicle Usage During Relocations,” published on March 26, 2024. GSA intends to revert the language in the FTR that was changed pursuant to FTR Case 2022-03 to the language that applied immediately prior to such changes; such predecessor language was agnostic as to the type of privately-owned vehicle owned or leased by a relocating employee.

records.Title: Federal Travel Regulation: Updating the FTR With Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language; Planned Rescission
records.Summary of Oppty: Announces intention to issue a Final Rule rescinding FTR Case 2022-05, titled “Updating the FTR With Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Language because the transgeder Eos require Federal agencies to recognize only two sexes, male and female, and take immediate action to effectuate the revocation of certain E.O.s which are not in line with the current Administration's priorities. Therefore, GSA will be reverting language in the FTR that was changed pursuant to FTR Case 2022-05, to sex-specific pronouns such as he, she, his, or her.

records.Title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Contract Year 2026 Policy and Technical Changes
records.Summary of Oppty: This final rule codifies certain Part D requirements from the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (IRA). Specifically, this rule codifies the IRA's vaccine and insulin cost-sharing requirements and codifies the program instruction for the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan program. Additionally, CMS is finalizing two IRA-related provisions that are needed to help ensure that selected drugs with maximum fair prices (MFPs) in effect under the Negotiation Program are available to beneficiaries at the point of dispensing and that the MFPs are effectuated for dispensing entities timely.

records.Title: Repeal of the Definition of Showerhead
records.Summary of Oppty: As part of its implementation of the Showerhead Executive order, the U.S. Department of Energy repeals the definition of a showerhead.

records.Title: Notice of Rescission of Guidance to Federal Financial Assistance Recipients Regarding Title VI Prohibition Against National Origin Discrimination Affecting Limited English Proficient Persons
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces DOJ's rescission of its Guidance to Federal Financial Assistance Recipients Regarding Title VI Prohibition Against National Origin Discrimination Affecting Limited English Proficient Persons, consistent with an Executive Order entitled Designating English as the Official Language of the United States. However, the notice reasserts that "Recipients of federal financial assistance, including subrecipients, are reminded that the denial of language assistance services can be evidence of discrimination on the basis of national origin or disability under certain circumstances."

records.Title: Rescission and Termination of the EIS Analyzing the Potential Environmental Effects From Maintaining Secretary Jewell's Coal Leasing Moratorium
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces the rescission of the Notice of Intent to prepare an environmental impact statement (EIS) and termination of the EIS analyzing the potential environmental effects from maintaining Secretary Jewell's coal leasing moratorium.

records.Title: Revokation: Protection of Marine Archeological Resources
records.Summary of Oppty: Under the Congressional Review Act, Congress passed, and the President signed, a joint resolution disapproving the final “Protection of Marine Archaeology Resources” rule published by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) on September 3, 2024. That rule required lessees and operators to submit an archaeological report with any oil and gas exploration or development plan they submit to BOEM for approval of proposed activities on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS).

records.Title: Marketplace Integrity and Affordability
records.Summary of Oppty: This proposed rule would revise standards relating to past-due premium payments; exclude Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients from the definition of “lawfully present”; the evidentiary standard HHS uses to assess potential noncompliance; failure to file and reconcile; income eligibility verifications for premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions; annual eligibility redetermination; the automatic reenrollment hierarchy; the annual open enrollment period; special enrollment periods; de minimis thresholds for plans subject to essential health benefits (EHB) requirements and for income-based cost-sharing reduction plan variations; and the premium adjustment percentage methodology; and prohibit issuers of coverage subject to EHB requirements from providing coverage for sex-trait modification as an EHB.

records.Title: Alien Registration Form and Evidence of Registration
records.Summary of Oppty: This IFR amends DHS regulations to designate a new registration form for undocumented people to comply with statutory registration and fingerprinting provisions. Undocumented people who are subject to registration requirements of the INA who have not yet registered may use this registration form to satisfy their statutory obligations. This IFR also amends DHS regulations to designate additional documentation that may serve as evidence of registration.

records.Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance; Clarification
records.Summary of Oppty: "Clarifies" that preamble language in an earlier HHS regulation that referred to gender dysphoria as a disability under section 504 of the ADA does not have the force of law and is therefore unenforceable.

records.Title: Notice of Designation of Policy-Making Positions
records.Summary of Oppty: Per EO 14171, FEC is designating the following positions as the Agency's confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating positions: Staff Director, General Counsel, Inspector General, and Director of Congressional and Intergovernmental Affairs.

records.Title: Implementation of the Commercial Advertisement Loudness Mitigation (CALM) Act
records.Summary of Oppty: This NPRM seeks input from consumers and industry on the extent to which the CALM Act rules have been effective in controlling and preventing loud commercials on programming provided by television broadcasters and pay TV providers. The Commission also asks about its authority to address loud commercials and the consistency of program volume on streaming platforms. Finally, the NPRM asks what actions the Commission, industry, or standards developers could take in this area to further minimize consumer harm.

records.Title: FY25 Final Sequestration Report
records.Summary of Oppty: This required yearly report affirms that, for fiscal year 2025, enacted appropriations are at or below the defense and non-defense caps after accounting for cap adjustments.

records.Title: Tier Fee Decrease for Our Electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification Service
records.Summary of Oppty: Reduces the fees for SSN verification. Notable because fees were adjusted in February and are substantially reduced here.

records.Title: State Data TA on IDEA Data Collection
records.Summary of Oppty: The purpose of the Technical Assistance on State Data Collection program is to improve the capacity of States to meet IDEA data collection and reporting requirements. Funding for the program is authorized under section 611(c)(1) of IDEA, which gives the Secretary authority to reserve not more than one-half of one percent of the amounts appropriated under Part B for each fiscal year to provide TA activities authorized under section 616(i), where needed, to improve the capacity of States to meet the data collection and reporting requirements under Parts B and C of IDEA.

records.Title: Comment Period Extension and Delay of Public Meetings
records.Summary of Oppty: Reopens the comment period on three rules regarding pollutants.

records.Title: Geographically Updated Population Certification Program
records.Summary of Oppty: Notice that the Census Bureau will modify the Geographically Updated Population Certification Program (GUPCP) by removing the expedited processing option for certified decennial census population and housing counts associated with updated government boundaries.

records.Title: Rescission of Policy Statement on Export Commencement Deadlines in Authorizations To Export Natural Gas to Non-Free Trade Agreement Countries
records.Summary of Oppty: DOE is responsible for authorizing exports of domestically produced natural gas, including liquefied natural gas (LNG), to foreign countries. In 2023, DOE issued a Policy Statement applying to existing and future authorizations for the export of natural gas to countries with which the United States does not have a free trade agreement (FTA) requiring national treatment for trade in natural gas and with which trade is not prohibited by U.S. law or policy (non-FTA countries). This notice rescinds that policy statement.

records.Title: Reconsideration of Disapproval Idaho Medicaid State Plan Amendment
records.Summary of Oppty: This notice announces an administrative hearing to reconsider CMS' decision to disapprove Idaho's Medicaid State Plan Amendment, which was submitted to CMS on October 11, 2024, and disapproved on January 6, 2025. This SPA proposed to elect the option authorized under section 1902(e)(16) of the Social Security Act (the Act) to provide continuous Medicaid coverage to pregnant Medicaid beneficiaries for the duration of their pregnancies and through the last day of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the last day of their pregnancies) ends. Idaho proposed in the SPA to exclude from its scope individuals whose pregnancies end due to abortions “that are not in accordance with Idaho Code 18-622" - Idaho's "criminal abortion" statute.

records.Title: Protecting Americans From Harmful Data Broker Practices
records.Summary of Oppty: The listing extends the comment period on a proposed rule that would implement the FCRA's definitions of consumer report and consumer reporting agency as well as certain of the FCRA's provisions governing when consumer reporting agencies may furnish, and users may obtain, consumer reports. The goal of the proposed rule is to restrict harmful uses of personal data, which it accomplishes by - among other things - restricting who can access credit reports, providing a right to contest info in a credit report, and requiring notifications when a landlord/employer/creditor relies on the report to make a negative determination about access to credit/housing/jobs/etc.
